title: fix: avoid TF32 matmul in camera frame orientation conversion

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+* Fixed :func:`~isaaclab.utils.math.convert_camera_frame_orientation_convention` returning NaN for the ``"world"``
+  convention when TF32 matmuls are enabled. The constant rotation is a signed column permutation and is now applied
+  without a matmul, so the result no longer depends on matmul precision.

@@ -1596,10 +1596,9 @@ def convert_camera_frame_orientation_convention(
     elif origin == "world":
         # convert from world (x forward and z up) to opengl convention
         rotm = matrix_from_quat(orientation)
-        rotm = torch.matmul(
-            rotm,
-            matrix_from_euler(torch.tensor([math.pi / 2, -math.pi / 2, 0], device=orientation.device), "XYZ"),
-        )
+        # right-multiply by the constant world <-> opengl rotation. It is a signed permutation of the columns, so
+        # it is applied without a matmul to stay exact when TF32 matmuls are enabled.
+        rotm = torch.stack([-rotm[..., 1], rotm[..., 2], -rotm[..., 0]], dim=-1)
         # convert to isaac-sim convention
         quat_gl = quat_from_matrix(rotm)
     else:
@@ -1615,10 +1614,8 @@ def convert_camera_frame_orientation_convention(
     elif target == "world":
         # convert from opengl to world (x forward and z up) convention
         rotm = matrix_from_quat(quat_gl)
-        rotm = torch.matmul(
-            rotm,
-            matrix_from_euler(torch.tensor([math.pi / 2, -math.pi / 2, 0], device=orientation.device), "XYZ").T,
-        )
+        # right-multiply by the constant opengl -> world rotation (a signed column permutation, see above)
+        rotm = torch.stack([-rotm[..., 2], -rotm[..., 0], rotm[..., 1]], dim=-1)
         return quat_from_matrix(rotm)
     else:
         return quat_gl.clone()

+def test_convention_converter(device, origin, target):
+    """Check camera conventions and input shapes against known rotations, including native CUDA TF32."""
+    previous_precision = torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision
+    try:
+        torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"
+        # Each convention describes the same two rotations; the second is the identity in ROS.
+        quats = {
+            "ros": torch.tensor(
+                [[0.33985114, 0.82047325, -0.42470819, -0.17591989], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]], device=device
+            ),
+            "opengl": torch.tensor(
+                [[0.17591988, 0.42470818, 0.82047324, 0.33985113], [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]], device=device
+            ),
+            "world": torch.tensor(
+                [[-0.27984815, -0.1159169, 0.88047623, -0.3647052], [0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5]], device=device
+            ),
+        }
+        # An asymmetric batch makes row-order errors visible across leading dimensions.
+        indices = [0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1]
+        quat = quats[origin][indices]
+        expected = quats[target][indices]
+        for orientation, expected_orientation in (
+            (quat, expected),
+            (quat.reshape(2, 4, 4), expected.reshape(2, 4, 4)),
+            (quat[0], expected[0]),
+        ):
+            actual = math_utils.convert_camera_frame_orientation_convention(orientation, origin, target)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected_orientation)
+    finally:
+        torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = previous_precision
